newsitem.title: UK: Conservatives still languishing in Scotland-poll.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives still languishing in Scotland-poll.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives have failed to make any headway with voters in Scotland, a traditional opposition Labour stronghold, an opinion poll in Monday's Scotsman newspaper showed.
The poll also showed that 71 percent of Scots want their own parliament, as proposed by Labour.

The poll, conducted by telephone from March 11-14, showed 47 percent of Scots intended to vote Labour, 23 percent favoured the pro-independence Scottish National Party, 17 percent the Conservatives and 10 percent the Liberal Democrats.
This means the Conservatives would lose seven of the 11 Scottish seats they won in the 1992 general election, while Labour would gain five to win 55 of the 72 Scottish seats, the Scotsman said.

Despite the strong support for a Scottish parliament, 75 percent of those polled said it would be unfair for Scottish members of the London parliament to be able to make decisions about English and Welsh affairs while English and Welsh MPs would have no say in Scottish matters.

The opposition Labour Party has pledged to introduce a separate Scottish parliament with tax-raising powers if it wins power, but the ruling Conservatives are determined to maintain the status quo, accusing Labour of threatening to break up the United Kingdom and impose a "Tartan Tax" on the Scots.
